artifacts.notes: 28663 LF-delimited physical lines. Uncorrected optical character recognition; it locates and identifies prayers and does not control wording.
artifacts.rights_basis: The underlying printing is in the public domain in the United States by publication date. The exact bytes registered here are an Internet Archive DjVuTXT optical-character-recognition derivative of that printing, and no distribution grant was established for the derivative itself or for the digitiser's own front matter where the file carries it. Triptych therefore records the exact remote bytes and their digest, retains no payload, and quotes from the underlying edition only what a locus needs.

edition.notes: The text preserves Carolingian orthography, folio marks in square brackets, and the e-caudata, which an optical text layer commonly renders as a caret or a question mark. A comparison must treat those as orthography and not as readings.
edition.publication: London: Henry Bradshaw Society, vol. XLIX, 1915. Edited by Henry Austin Wilson from Cambrai 164 with two further ninth-century manuscripts.
edition.title: The Gregorian Sacramentary under Charles the Great, edited from three MSS. of the ninth century by H. A. Wilson

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The papal sacramentary sent by Hadrian I to Charlemagne, transmitted with the supplement long ascribed to Alcuin. It is the immediate ancestor of the medieval and Tridentine Roman Mass books and the second great reservoir the twentieth-century reform drew its orations from.
work.title: Sacramentarium Gregorianum (Hadrianum)
